newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares relieved by Wall Street end higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares relieved by Wall Street end higher.

text.p: Israeli shares closed slightly higher on Tuesday in thin trading following Wall Street's recovery overnight, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.34 percent, or 0.99 points, to 295.67 on low all-share turnover of 147 million shekels against 161 million shekels on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.31 percent higher at 304.07.
"Investors are more relaxed now after the recovery of Wall Street on Monday, but activity is still relatively low," said Doron Tsur, head of research at Sahar Securities.

"Volume is still low because investors are waiting to see what will happen in the U.S. market. I think the market will continue to be very nervous until Wall Street stabilises," said Michael Weiss at Evergreen Capital Markets.
He said expectations for an interest rate hike next week would also shadow the market. Expectations are for an increase of up to 0.5 percentage point on the current 12.7 percent base rate.

Tsur said the market's direction was also riding on second-quarter earnings. "Until now, the reports were more or less within expectations, but usually the good reports are the first to be released," he said.
He added that the recent surge in convertible bond offerings is hurting the trading volume. "The new issues suck money from the stock market," he said.

First International Bank of Israel rose 2.25 percent to 268,595 agorot (Israeli cents). The bank on Tuesday reported second-quarter earnings per share of 10.59 shekels against 8.54 shekels at the same quarter last year.
Clal Electronic Industries gained 0.25 percent to 52,034 agorot. Clal said on Tuesday that second-quarter net profit surged to 122.4 million shekels from 17 million shekels a year earlier.
Dead Sea Bromine lost 0.5 percent to 2,507 agorot. Sahar Securities and Investments upgraded Dead Sea to a buy from a hold after the company reported better-than-expected second-quarter results.
Sahar set a 12-month price target of 28 to 30 shekels for the shares.

The most active shares were Bank Hapoalim, which fell 1.25 percent to 766 agorot on volume of 7.6 million shekels; Koor Industries, which gained 0.5 percent to 36,991 agorot on volume of 7.3 million shekels; and Tadiran which lost 1.5 percent to 11,521 agorot on turnover of seven million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
